title: Juniper and the Safehouse
premise: Xanthe Okafor, a former intelligence linguist turned interpreter for a doomed peace delegation, has spent six years hiding inside a handler-built identity, keeping a go-bag packed and his real name buried. When the safehouse that anchors his cover life is listed online with interior photos — his books, his photographs, his mother's chair — he realizes the network that trained him is selling him out to the delegation's saboteurs. To survive, Xanthe must turn hunter: dismantling the cell that made him while deciding whether loyalty belongs to the found family he built in hiding or the truth he's been paid to bury. The story ends with Xanthe exposing the network's ledger at the collapsed peace talks, burning his old identity for good, and walking away not into witness protection but into the chosen family who finally knows his real name.
about_author: Theo Marchetti is the pen name of a former NGO field coordinator who spent a decade in contested border regions before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people whose professional fluency in deception collides with their hunger to be known.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Scrolling property listings at 2 a.m., he finds the safehouse for sale — every room photographed, including the hidden compartment behind his bookshelf. He recognizes the staging choices as a message, not an accident. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath practiced calm; the lie he polished for six years just went public.

chapters.title: Go-Bag Protocol
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. He runs extraction protocol but hesitates at the door — leaving means abandoning Juniper, the teenage runaway he's quietly sheltered, and the delegation mid-negotiation. A burner call from his old handler, Voss, confirms someone inside the network leaked the listing. Beat: loyalty pulling against survival instinct.

chapters.title: Interpreting the Enemy
chapters.summary: Delegation POV through Xanthe's ears. During translation sessions he catches a delegate using a phrase only network-trained operatives use — the sabotage is seated at the table. He must translate faithfully while signaling nothing. Beat: the vertigo of hearing betrayal rendered in two languages.

chapters.title: Juniper
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She's noticed Xanthe's midnight rituals — the bag, the maps, the second phone — and confronts him with her own secret: she ran from a family connected to the same network. Two liars recognize each other. Beat: wary tenderness; the first crack in his isolation.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Xanthe meets Voss in a rail station café. Voss claims the listing was a rogue element, offers Xanthe reinstatement and protection — if he identifies the mole at the talks. Xanthe realizes he's being handled again. Beat: the seductive pull of belonging to the thing that trained you.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Xanthe breaks into the network's dead-drop archive and retrieves the ledger — years of sold identities, including delegates' families. But the break-in was anticipated; his exit route collapses and he barely escapes, wounded. Beat: no more half-measures; the past has teeth.

chapters.title: House of Photos
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. While Xanthe recovers, she decodes the listing photos and finds the timestamp metadata points to someone still living in the safehouse — a caretaker, or a trap. They stake it out together and find the 'buyer' photographing rooms on schedule. Beat: found family forged under surveillance.

chapters.title: The Vote That Fails
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The delegation's final session collapses exactly on schedule; the operative delegate triggers the walkout. In the chaos, Xanthe chooses truth over cover, publicly confronting the operative in three languages until the room understands. Beat: climax — loyalty to truth finally outweighs the polished lie.

chapters.title: Burning the Network
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Using the ledger and the operative's confession, he feeds the network's structure to journalists and prosecutors, then sends Voss one last message: the student is done being inventory. Voss's reply is a single word — respect. Beat: catharsis with a cost; his old name is now public record.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Xanthe and Juniper. Weeks later, they buy the safehouse themselves — legally, openly — and unpack the go-bag for the first time, item by item, telling each other what each object really means. Beat: resolution; invisibility traded for belonging, the packed bag replaced by a home.
